messages:
Sam: quick Q — where do I look for TTFT / tokens/sec + p95/p99 for inference? trying to correlate a user report with a spike in token throughput.
Mira: Grafana is your friend here. go to Grafana -> Dashboards -> 'Infra / Inference / Latency & Throughput' (we put the TTFT and tokens panels in that folder). link: https://grafana.internal.company/d/INF_LATENCY
Chris: Prometheus queries if you want raw numbers:

- p95 latency (5m window, grouped by model):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, model))
```

- p99 similarly with 0.99

- tokens/sec (1m window, per model):
```
sum(rate(llm_tokens_emitted_total{job="inference"}[1m])) by (model)
```

Those are what our Grafana panels use. replace `model` with `route` if you're correlating frontend routes.
Mira: for TTFT (time-to-first-token) we derive from traces and a metric. Two options:
1) traces: Tempo/OpenTelemetry — search span name "first_token" and filter by service=inference. go to https://tempo.internal.company/trace/explore and set span.name=first_token
2) metric: `redwood_ttft_seconds` (ingested from spans) — basic query:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_ttft_seconds_bucket{job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, model))
```

We push both to the dashboard so you can eyeball traces where TTFT is high and then jump to logs.
Anita: logs live in Loki under the "inference" app label. quick Loki examples:
```
{app="inference"} |= "first_token" | unwrap duration_sec | sort_desc(duration_sec)
```
or to find timeouts:
```
{app="inference", level="error"} |= "timeout"
```

Those will link back to traces if trace IDs are present in the log lines.
Sam: awesome, do we have an existing alert for TTFT p95? user hit a slow spike earlier and no pager.
Chris: yes — alert name is INF_TTFT_P95_HIGH in PrometheusRules, lives in `infra-alerts` config. Rule looks like:
```
alert: INF_TTFT_P95_HIGH
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_ttft_seconds_bucket{job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, model)) > 0.8
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "TTFT p95 > 800ms for {{ $labels.model }}"
```
We historically set 0.8s as the SLO breach threshold, but plenty of model variants need higher thresholds.
Mira: if it's noisy, raise threshold per-model; we have overrides in `infra-alerts/overrides.yaml` — add a regexp for model name and new threshold, then open a PR. ops will approve faster if you include traffic % and customer impact in the PR description.
Anita: FYI we recently added a tokens/sec soft alert (INF_TOKENS_RATE_HIGH) that fires when tokens/sec > X sustained for 5m. This is to catch runaway loops. It is a warn-level alert (pager=false) but notifies #eng-sre.
Sam: can someone paste the exact panels I should look at? want to share with product PM.
Mira: panels (in the INF_LATENCY dashboard):
- "TTFT p50/p95/p99 by model" (panel id 4)
- "Request latency histogram" (panel id 7)
- "Tokens/sec by model" (panel id 11)
- "Active inflight requests" (panel id 14)
Use the time picker +/- 30m around the incident and set $__rate_interval to 1m for tokens.
Chris: when correlating, do this order:
1) tokens/sec spike
2) TTFT rises shortly after (if caused by backend backpressure)
3) traces: increase in first_token span durations
4) logs: look for queue/backpressure/timeouts

If you want, paste the trace id here and I can jump in.
Sam: got it. I'll pull the dashboard and paste a trace id if I see one.
observability-bot: Saved dashboard link: https://grafana.internal.company/d/INF_LATENCY?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now
Anita: small tip — for quick ad-hoc PromQL you can use Grafana Explore with the following to show p95 across models as a table:
```
label_replace(
  topk(25, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))),
  "model", "$1", "model", "(.+)"
)
```
Sam: thanks everyone. i'll file a runbook PR if this was customer-facing. pinging @Chris if you can help with thresholds.
Chris: will review the PR. if we need per-model thresholds, we'll add an annotation explaining why.
Sam: thanks :thumbsup:
Mira: FYI i'll also add a small note in the runbook about checking the per-model quota/burst config — sometimes tokens/sec spikes are due to a downstream retry loop.
Sam: perfect. closing this thread after I confirm.
